key_insight: A large open-weight LLM (Llama 3.3 70B) can accurately identify PCI reports and extract key complex PCI features from unstructured cath notes, outperforming smaller domain-specific models.
clinical_relevance: This could enable scalable, locally deployable phenotyping for cardiovascular research by reducing manual chart abstraction workload.
method: Evaluated Llama 3.3 70B, Meditron-7B, and BioMistral-7B on manually annotated catheterization reports from three hospitals.
Tested two tasks: PCI report identification and extraction of six complex PCI variables.
Compared model outputs against human annotations across site-level subsets.
evidence_signal: Across 1,412 notes, 596 were PCI reports; Llama 3.3 70B reached 100.0% sensitivity and 93.8% specificity for PCI identification, and 97.7% sensitivity with 83.9% accuracy for complex PCI classification in 590 evaluable PCI reports.
watch_item: Performance varied by site and was weaker for variables requiring interpretation across multiple procedural details, so local validation and careful deployment are important.
paper_title: Automated Identification of Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention from Cardiac Catheterization Reports Using Large Language Models
